lesson_title: Climate and Geomorphology Essentials: The Paper 1 Revision Sweep
hook_text: Two cyclones, one chart, three seconds to tell them apart. Here's the check the examiners can't trick.
clip_script: On a synoptic chart the three are unmistakable if you check three things: an L with fronts attached is a mid-latitude cyclone; a tight, nearly circular swirl in the tropics with no fronts is a tropical cyclone; a broad H with widely spaced isobars is an anticyclone. A mid-latitude cyclone lives south of the country and drags a line of triangles for the cold front. A tropical cyclone has no fronts at all, because it is built from one warm air mass, not from two fighting ones — its isobars are almost perfect circles packed around a deep centre. Latitude, fronts, isobars. Run those three looks in order and you cannot confuse them.
visual_style: Split-screen synoptic chart sketch: left, a frontal low with triangles and half-moons south of the Cape; right, a tight tropical swirl in the Mozambique Channel — a big checklist stamping LATITUDE, FRONTS, ISOBARS over each in turn.
pacing: Three quick beats for the three checks, then a slow confident close on the full chart.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision session and sweep all of Paper 1's theory in one sitting.
